notes: Lightest of the molasses sugars: sotolon-dominant 'clean caramel'. The OTHER Maillard products (pyrazines, furans, pyrroles) that mark brown sugar and muscovado are minimal here — sotolon-alone is the citable distinguishing feature, not an unfinished profile. Distinct from white sugar (no aroma) and from brown sugar (which adds the roasty layer).
source: Tokitomo et al., Proc. Japan Acad. Ser. B 1980, 56(7):457 (sotolon = key odorant of raw cane sugar). See research log.

notes: Whole unrefined cane, long-boiled with all molasses + minerals retained. Phenolic peat-smoke note: the family of compounds peat-fire kilning deposits on malted barley. Guaiacol is the highest-flavour-intensity member; phenol/cresol/ethyl- and vinyl-guaiacol fill out the medicinal/smoky character. Flavour-source proxy (not a literal ingredient), used to give peated whisky its distinguishing profile.
source: Direct-injection MS and SBSE/LVI-GC-MS quantitation of phenolics in Islay single malts (Fraunhofer / The Analytical Scientist); guaiacol, 4-ethylguaiacol, 4-vinylguaiacol, cresols, phenol identified as the dominant peat odorants.

notes: Filbertone (E-alpha-filbertone, 5-methyl-4-heptanone) is the defining hazelnut odorant; benzaldehyde gives the shared almond-like note; pyrazine covers the roasted/toasted character. Flavour-source proxy for hazelnut-forward liqueurs.
source: Hazelnut aroma chemistry: filbertone identified as species-specific odorant (Corylus avellana); GC-MS literature on roasted hazelnut volatiles (Manzocco et al.; NIST Flavor database).

notes: Phenolic hardwood-smoke note from pit/charcoal roasting (the agave-pit step in mezcal; also lapsang, smoked salt, smoked paprika). Guaiacol + cresol are the markers that separate mezcal from tequila; 4-ethylguaiacol adds the creosote edge. Syringol and 4-methylguaiacol are the hardwood-lignin signature — present in wood smoke but largely absent from peat smoke, so wood_smoke and peat_smoke share three compounds (a real chemical bridge) without collapsing into each other. Flavour-source proxy, not a literal ingredient. Smoke intensity is a production-style variable (degree/duration of roast), not an agave-variety trait; this models the smoky baseline of the category.
source: Mezcal GC-MS/SPME volatile profiling (Vera Guzmán et al., MDPI Beverages 2018; De León-Rodríguez et al., Agave salmiana mezcal); guaiacol & cresol identified as the smoke markers differentiating mezcal from tequila. Smoke-phenol sensory descriptors (guaiacol clove/smoky; 4-ethylguaiacol smoky/creosote; syringol & 4-methylguaiacol woody/ashy) per Hsu & Yu, Molecules 2018 (PMC6017423).

notes: Distinct from sweet orange: keeps the limonene/linalool/octanal citrus base but adds a red-berry/floral layer. beta-damascenone carries the rose/berry/brambly/cherry character (the 'blood' note), beta-ionone the violet/hibiscus floral, decanal the rich peel aldehyde. This is what lets blood orange bridge into the berry, stone-fruit and grape families (cognac, PX/port, cherry, apricot, raspberry) that plain orange can't. AU season ~Sept-Nov (early spring); flagged provisional on the norisoprenoid assignment.
source: Flavour descriptor profile (Flavonomics: red berry, brambly, cherry-like, rosy, violic, apricoty, hibiscine over a limonene citrus base; documented port/raisin and vanilla synergies). Compound assignment: limonene/linalool/octanal from Citrus sinensis peel oil; beta-damascenone + beta-ionone (norisoprenoids) assigned to the red-berry/violet notes; decanal a documented blood-orange peel aldehyde. PROVISIONAL — norisoprenoid levels not GC-MS-verified for this entry.

notes: Citrus bergamia peel oil — the scent in Earl Grey / Lady Grey tea. Linalyl acetate + linalool give the floral-citrus signature (shared with lavender); limonene/beta-pinene/gamma-terpinene the bright citrus. Bridges blood orange (linalool/limonene), lavender (linalyl acetate) and the gin/amaro citrus family. NOTE: as a proxy for Earl Grey/Lady Grey it models only the bergamot AROMA — black tea's tannin/astringency (a real structural/leather contribution) is a non-volatile taste-active outside Cobber's aroma-only compound vocabulary.
source: Citrus bergamia cold-pressed peel oil GC profiles (linalyl acetate ~30%, limonene ~30-40%, linalool ~10%, gamma-terpinene, beta-pinene); standard bergamot essential-oil composition.
